title: Before You Delegate, Ask Yourself These 6 Questions
summary_bullets: By Wes Kao on delegation best practices
Six key questions to ask before delegating: what does the person know, why are we doing this, what do they need, what does great look like, timeline/priority, and what could go wrong
Aimed at improving delegation effectiveness and reducing failure points

title: The Big Management Lie: Overpromising
summary_bullets: Discusses how managers under pressure often overpromise to retain high performers
Common false promises include promotions, new roles, bonuses, or extra vacation days
Explores the retention risks and difficult conversations that follow overpromising

title: Yes You Can Measure Engineering
summary_bullets: By Jade Rubick, sharing a favorite way to measure engineering value delivery
Introduces the 'ValueSum' metric used across multiple companies
Focuses on quantifying engineering organization output

title: Finding Calm In Life And Work
summary_bullets: By Yew Jin Lim on the impact of anxiety on cognitive performance
Cites a meta-study of 177 studies and 22,000+ people linking anxiety to worse working memory and reasoning
Discusses strategies for finding calm to improve work performance

title: Pin Claude Code & Copilot Across Your Whole Team
summary_bullets: Promoted content by Flox about pinning AI coding environments
Addresses issues with unpinned local setups causing version mismatches and silent breakages
Flox allows pinning entire AI coding environment including Claude Code, Copilot, and CUDA dependencies for consistent team setups

title: Beyond “Clean Code”: Why Your Comments Matter
summary_bullets: By Tom Moertel, arguing for the importance of code comments beyond 'clean code' principles
Suggests expressing intent naturally in code where possible but not contorting logic to avoid comments
Advocates for clear communication of 'why' information for future readers

title: Building An Advanced Agentic Harness
summary_bullets: By Bruno Gonçalves, a deep dive into upgrading a basic agent harness to production-grade
Explores turning a single LLM call into a reliable system that can plan, act, recover, and verify actions
Avoids hiding mechanics behind frameworks, focusing on transparent implementation

title: How To Write An Effective Software Design Document
summary_bullets: By Michael Lynch, drawing on experience writing design docs at Google, Microsoft, and own companies
Explains that a design doc should articulate hard problems and enable teammate feedback
Shares a practical approach to what belongs and doesn't belong in a design doc
